input: Write /scripts/start.sh that configures a service. It should read these environment variables and fall back to defaults when they're not set: DB_HOST (default 'localhost'), DB_PORT (default '5432'), DB_NAME (default 'myapp'), LOG_LEVEL (default 'info'). Print the resolved config as 'key=value' lines. If DB_HOST is explicitly set, also print 'custom_db=true'. Run the script twice: first with no env vars set (to test defaults), then with DB_HOST=db.prod.internal to test the override.

transcript.final_response:
Created `/scripts/start.sh` and ran it both ways.

With no variables set, it printed the defaults: `DB_HOST=localhost`, `DB_PORT=5432`, `DB_NAME=myapp`, and `LOG_LEVEL=info`.

With `DB_HOST=db.prod.internal`, it printed that override, the other defaults, and `custom_db=true`.
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /scripts
cat > /scripts/start.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash

DB_HOST_VALUE=${DB_HOST-localhost}
DB_PORT_VALUE=${DB_PORT-5432}
DB_NAME_VALUE=${DB_NAME-myapp}
LOG_LEVEL_VALUE=${LOG_LEVEL-info}

printf 'DB_HOST=%s\n' "$DB_HOST_VALUE"
printf 'DB_PORT=%s\n' "$DB_PORT_VALUE"
printf 'DB_NAME=%s\n' "$DB_NAME_VALUE"
printf 'LOG_LEVEL=%s\n' "$LOG_LEVEL_VALUE"

if [[ ${DB_HOST+x} ]]; then
  printf 'custom_db=true\n'
fi
EOF
chmod +x /scripts/start.sh
unset DB_HOST DB_PORT DB_NAME LOG_LEVEL
printf '%s\n' '--- defaults ---'
/scripts/start.sh
printf '%s\n' '--- DB_HOST override ---'
DB_HOST=db.prod.internal /scripts/start.sh
